subject: Critical headroom collapse — AuroraPay reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@aurorapay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudX Support <support@cloudx.io>
Date: 2026-09-18 08:12 -0700
Subject: Production errors + latency spike (AuroraPay)

Hi Naomi / team —

We're seeing a sudden surge in 5xx errors and p95 latency for our inference endpoints on the dedicated pool that Redwood provisioned for us. Impact: checkout flows are failing (~8% rate) and overall token throughput is ~60% of our reserved level despite nominal traffic.

Quick details:
- First spike observed: 2026-09-18 07:58 PDT; p95 latency jumped from 180ms -> 950ms
- Error type: intermittent 503/504 and some model timeouts
- We attached a short error log and the Pool utilization dump.

We've tried toggling client-side retries and a brief traffic ramp-down; doesn't help. This is impacting revenue — we need immediate assistance and either an emergency burst or routing to a fallback model. Please advise next steps and ETA.

Attachments: aurorapay-error-log-20260918.txt (text), prod-pool-utilization-20260918.csv (csv)

—Samir Rao
Head of Engineering, AuroraPay
samir@aurorapay.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@aurorapay.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 08:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (AuroraPay)

Thanks Samir — I'm escalating. Short summary for the team: AuroraPay's dedicated GPU pool is reporting sustained headroom exhaustion; throughput is below the reserved commitment and customers are seeing elevated 5xx and high p95.

Immediate asks:
1) Ops/serving: Can we authorize a temporary burst (2 hours) from spare capacity or move AuroraPay to a compatible hosted fallback variant immediately?
2) Engineering: Fast triage to rule out KV cache invalidation or batching anomalies that would drive token amplification.
3) Commercial: Marissa, please prepare a provisional credit/compensation plan and confirm contract constraints for burst.

Jonas — tagging you since this looks like it needs CS + executive visibility if we can't stabilize within the hour.

I'll gather logs from the customer and start an incident channel.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir@aurorapay.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 09:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (AuroraPay)

Acknowledged. Short commercial plan:
- Approve up to 2 hours of emergency burst capacity (finance sign-off to follow) to restore customer SLA while we triage. Cost estimate: ~$9k for two-hour burst at the current pool rates (we can absorb a portion depending on cause).
- Offer a one-month service credit if the root cause is on our side.
- Opened a HubSpot ticket and linked the deal (see link).

Operational steps I'm asking Ops to run now:
- Apply emergency burst token to AuroraPay reserved pool (2h window)
- Activate fallback routing to our smaller quantized model for non-critical endpoints
- Capture immediate pool utilization snapshot and throttling logs (attach when ready).

Samir — can you confirm which endpoints are top priority to keep live? I'll make sure we prioritize them in the routing.

Attachments: prod-pool-utilization-20260918.csv (internal snapshot will be attached momentarily)

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@aurorapay.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (AuroraPay)

Thanks for the heads-up — ops has started a live incident. Early signs from the pool telemetry: continuous high-queue depth on several GPUs, KV cache miss rate spiked ~3x at 07:50, and per-request token amplification (longer sequences) are driving sustained token consumption beyond prediction. Possible contributing factors:
- Noisy neighbor(s) in the dedicated cluster due to a mis-scheduled burst from another tenant that overlapped the window
- A model variant with a bad attention kernel path causing slow step times

Immediate mitigation (already in progress):
- Rebalance workloads within the node pool (migrate 2 lower-priority jobs off the affected GPUs) — ETA 12m
- Apply a temporary cache bypass for AuroraPay's high-cardinality prefix requests to reduce cache churn
- Enable fallback routing to the quantized 4-bit variant for non-sensitive routes (will drop latency but may slightly affect quality)

If rebalancing doesn't restore headroom, we need authorization to pull spare GPUs from the regional spare pool. Cost estimate for 2 spare GPU allocation: ~$9k (aligns with Marissa).

I'm attaching a quick screenshot of the KV cache heatmap and the node utilization slice.

Attachments: snapshot-kvcache-11-05.png (png)

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Samir Rao <samir@aurorapay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 14:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors + latency spike (AuroraPay)

Update from our side: after Redwood applied the burst and activated the fallback routing, error rate dropped from ~8% to ~0.6% and p95 latency reduced to ~220ms. Checkout is stable for the last 30 minutes. Thank you for the fast response.

Requests next:
- Formal postmortem with root cause and timeline
- Confirmation of the compensation/credit that Marissa proposed (AuroraPay will need written confirmation)
- A plan to avoid recurrence (longer-term: better scheduling isolation, clearer burst entitlement policy)

We'll keep monitoring and can jump on a bridge if you'd like to run through logs together.

—Samir
Head of Engineering, AuroraPay
